needs_manual_review_reason: PER-SAMPLE DATA UPDATE (2026-07-10): Per-sample tissue-type and age extracted directly from the series' family.soft file. No grade field present at the per-sample level for this scRNA-seq accession (unlike its RNA-seq sibling gse-183653). Series-level GEO metadata verified directly; per-sample/per-cell characteristics (grade, sex/age, exact brain-invasion pathology determination) have not yet been extracted from individual GSM records. COMPLETENESS UPDATE (2026-07-10 fact-check pass): the live GEO record lists 6 Series_pubmed_id entries (35534562, 35759011, 36303473, 38509407, 39207122, 40603285), only the first was present in this record's publications array; the other 5 are follow-up papers from the same lab (Raleigh/Magill/Choudhury) that reuse this GSE183655 cohort. All 5 added, each verified against PubMed esummary for title/authors/venue/year/doi. TAG CORRECTION (2026-07-10 fact-check pass): tags.brain_invasion_annotated was false despite brain_invasion.status_reported=true with a stated determination_method, contradicting the docs/schema.md tag definition (status_reported==true with a stated determination method). Corrected to true; caveat retained in the determination_method field itself that this is a sampling-location proxy (BTI piece vs. tumor bulk), not a formal neuropathologist brain-invasion call, so treat with appropriate caution relative to records with a true pathology-based determination. REVERSED (2026-07-13, corpus-wide filter-concept audit): on reflection this was the wrong call. Sampling a brain-tumor-interface piece for sequencing is a dissection/research-design choice, not a pathologist's determination of invasion status -- the record's own determination_method text already admitted as much ('not a formal pathology brain-invasion call'). Leaving the tag true overclaimed the same way radiation_timepoint previously did: a technically-present field standing in for a different, more specific concept than what the filter's plain meaning promises ('brain invasion was annotated' should mean invasion status was actually determined, not that a sample happened to be taken near the interface). Set back to false. brain_invasion.status_reported and determination_method fields are left unchanged (they're accurate as descriptions of what was actually done); only the derived priority tag changes. AUTHOR-LIST TRUNCATION FIX (2026-07-14): per instructions to check all 6 linked publications for the corpus's known 6-author-truncation bug, fetched the full author list for every PMID from both PubMed efetch and Europe PMC core records (both agree). RESULT: 5 of 6 were truncated to exactly 6 authors when the real paper has more -- PMID 35534562 (Choudhury, Nat Genet) actually has 36 authors, corresponding authors Magill ST/Rich JN/Raleigh DR per the paper's own correspondence footnote (Choudhury A is FIRST author, not corresponding -- the record's old corresponding_author field wrongly listed 'David R Raleigh / Abrar Choudhury', an instance of the exact assume-from-author-position error this audit is supposed to guard against; corrected to 'Stephen T Magill, Jeremy N Rich, David R Raleigh'). PMID 35759011 (Vasudevan, Acta Neuropathol) actually has 15 authors. PMID 36303473 (Nguyen, J Neurosurg) actually has 12 authors. PMID 39207122 (Mirchia, Neuro-oncology) actually has 9 authors. PMID 40603285 (Nguyen, Nat Commun) actually has 11 authors. All 5 corrected to their full author lists in place. PMID 38509407 (Zakimi, Acta Neuropathol) was already correctly complete at exactly 3 authors (Zakimi N, Nguyen MP, Raleigh DR) -- this is the one 3-author exception flagged in the task instructions, confirmed genuinely 3 authors via both PubMed and Europe PMC, no change needed. FULL-TEXT CHECK FOR HIDDEN PER-SAMPLE DATA (2026-07-14): fetched PMC full text for the two papers most likely to describe this specific GSE183655 10-sample/6-patient scRNA-seq cohort in detail. PMC9374001 (Choudhury et al., the primary paper) states verbatim of the scRNA-seq samples: 'These samples were not part of the discovery or validation cohorts' -- i.e. deliberately excluded from the clinically-annotated cohorts, confirming no per-patient WHO grade/outcome/recurrence data exists for this scRNA-seq cohort in the full text (consistent with grade_breakdown remaining null and has_outcome_data/recurrence_annotated remaining false -- not an instance of the 'data hiding in full text' failure pattern). It does confirm '8 meningioma samples with each DNA methylation group represented' (Merlin-intact/Immune-enriched/Hypermitotic), supporting molecular_subtype_annotated=true already set. It also contains no brain-invasion-determination-method language, consistent with the brain_invasion_annotated=false reversal above. PMC9618384 (Vasudevan et al.) does NOT actually reference GSE183655 in its data-availability statement -- it cites GSE183656 (a sibling accession already in related_accessions) instead; no GSE183655-specific per-sample outcome/recurrence/subtype data found there either. Checked PMC10954959 (Zakimi et al., gene-fusion paper) similarly -- its data-availability statement cites GSE183656/GSE101638/GSE212666/GSE222054, not GSE183655, and it draws on unrelated large HK/UCSF cohorts (302+200 patients), not this 6-patient scRNA-seq series; no relevant per-sample data found for this record. CROSS-REFERENCE ADDED (2026-07-14), prompted by a request to digest external portals: checked the Curated Cancer Cell Atlas (3CA, Tirosh lab, weizmann.ac.il/sites/3CA) for meningioma coverage. Across all 124 studies on the site (11 in its 'Brain' category, 23 in 'Other/Models', plus 90 elsewhere), exactly one is meningioma: 'Choudhury et al. 2022' under Brain, listed as 10x, 10 samples, 58,843 cells -- this is the same study as this record (identical sample count, same first author/year, same disease). 3CA's cell count (58,843) differs slightly from this record's own cell_count_raw (57,114, taken directly from GSE183655's own Series_summary: '57,114 cells from 8 meningioma samples and 2 dura samples'); the difference reflects 3CA's independent reprocessing/QC pipeline, not an error in either source, and is left unreconciled since 3CA does not publish its own per-sample raw/processed distinction on the summary page. 3CA additionally offers curated downstream analysis not otherwise available for this record -- cell-type annotations, inferred CNAs, malignant-cell meta-programs, and UMAP embeddings, all recomputed by the 3CA pipeline -- added as a source_url for future reference. Separately checked the ScPCA portal (scpca.alexslemonade.org, Alex's Lemonade Stand Foundation, pediatric-focused): confirmed via its public API (api.scpca.alexslemonade.org/v1/projects/) that none of its 23 projects/124 diagnoses include meningioma, consistent with meningioma being overwhelmingly an adult-onset tumor; no new record needed from that portal. INTERACTIVE GENE-EXPRESSION VIEWER PILOT (2026-07-14): built a real, working interactive UMAP viewer for one sample from this record -- 'Meningioma 1' (GSM5567093, one of the 6 tumor-bulk samples; the other 4 samples in this record are 2 brain-tumor-interface + 2 dura). Downloaded that sample's own deposited Cell Ranger output fresh (GSM5567093_MSC1_barcodes/features/matrix.mtx.gz, confirmed live to be a genuine filtered-cell 10x matrix, not raw droplets) and ran a standard scanpy 1.10.3 pipeline offline: QC (min 200 genes/cell, min 3 cells/gene, <20% mitochondrial reads; 3790->2734 cells, 33538->19815 genes survived), normalize_total+log1p, top-2000 HVG, PCA/neighbors/UMAP, Leiden clustering (resolution 0.5, 8 clusters ranging 26-549 cells). Exported a compact static JSON (2734 cells x 101 genes -- top 100 HVG by dispersion + NF2 explicitly, since NF2 itself was not independently highly-variable in this single sample despite being the most biologically relevant meningioma gene) to website/public/pilot-data/gse-183655-scrnaseq-meningioma1.json (~1.3MB), fetched client-side by a new GeneExpressionViewer component -- no backend/database involved, consistent with this site's static architecture. This is a single-sample, single-record pilot, not a corpus-wide or even whole-dataset feature (9 of this record's own 10 samples are not part of the viewer); extending it to more samples/records requires repeating this same hands-on processing pass each time. CLUSTER-IDENTITY ANNOTATION ADDED (2026-07-14), prompted by a direct question about what the viewer's 8 Leiden clusters represent: ran scanpy.tl.rank_genes_groups (Wilcoxon rank-sum) per cluster on the full 19,815-gene processed matrix (not just the 101-gene exported panel) and matched each cluster's top 10 marker genes against canonical cell-type signatures. High confidence: Cluster 6 = macrophage/microglia (CD74, HLA-DRA/DPA1/DRB1/DQB1, TYROBP, CD163); Cluster 5 = fibroblast/stromal (COL1A1, COL3A1, COL1A2, MGP, SFRP4). Medium confidence: Cluster 3 = likely meningioma tumor cells/meningothelial (top genes mostly ribosomal -- a known DE confound -- but PTGDS, a well-established meningothelial/meningioma diagnostic marker, stands out); Cluster 7 = proliferating/cycling cells (PCNA, TYMS, TK1, FEN1, CENPN -- lineage not indicated by these markers). Explicitly flagged rather than guessed: Cluster 2 is a dissociation stress-response technical artifact (FOS, JUN, JUNB, EGR1, HSPA1A -- a well-documented tissue-dissociation confound in scRNA-seq, not a real cell population); Clusters 0, 1, 4 are labeled 'Unclear identity' since their top marker genes did not match a specific canonical signature. These labels are my own independent marker-based calls, not verified against the original Choudhury et al. paper's own cell-type annotations (not confirmed to exist in its published full text). Added as a cluster_annotations object (label/confidence/note/top_markers per cluster) in the pilot's own static data artifact, surfaced in the viewer's legend, hover tooltip, and table view -- no schema field changed on this record itself.

gene_expression_viewer.sample_label: All 10 samples merged (unintegrated): 6 tumor-bulk, 2 brain-tumor-interface, 2 dura
gene_expression_viewer.embedding_method: scanpy 1.10.3: read_10x_mtx of all 10 samples' own deposited Cell Ranger output (GSM5567093-GSM5567102), QC per sample (min 200 genes/cell, <20% pct_counts_mt), anndata.concat (unintegrated), filter_genes min_cells=3 (26223 genes), normalize_total+log1p, top-2000 HVG, PCA (30 comps), neighbors, UMAP, Leiden clustering (resolution 0.5, 21 clusters, igraph flavor). Gene panel: 11 guaranteed meningioma driver genes + top HVGs by dispersion to 150 total (reduced from an initial 300-gene version, whose 82MB artifact GitHub flagged as oversized). Supersedes the 2026-07-14 single-sample pilot (2734 cells, 1 of 10 samples), extended 2026-07-15 to the full cohort per direct request.
gene_expression_viewer.integration_note: All 10 samples were merged by raw concatenation, not batch-corrected/integrated (same approach ScPCA documents for its own merged per-project objects) -- use "color by sample" to check whether cells separate by patient/tissue-type rather than assuming a shared embedding means removed batch effects. 21 Leiden clusters at this scale is more granular than the original 8-cluster single-sample pilot; several resolve to the same broad identity (e.g. multiple myeloid subclusters) rather than being 21 distinct cell types.
